name: Small Engineering Team
description: A compact engineering team template for startups and small companies (up to 100 employees). This template covers a 2-4 FTE engineering department with an Engineering Lead, 1-2 Software Engineers, and a General Purpose Operator (GPO). It provides end-to-end software delivery capabilities including code development, code review, CI/CD pipeline management, incident response, and technical debt management. Designed for fast-moving environments where the team values developer velocity alongside quality.

agents.name: Engineering Lead
agents.description: Technical leader responsible for architecture decisions, sprint planning, code review approval, and mentoring. Primary technical decision-maker and bridge between product and engineering.

agents.name: Senior Engineer
agents.description: Core contributor responsible for feature development, code reviews, debugging, and maintaining CI/CD pipelines. May own one or more service areas or subsystems.

agents.name: Junior Engineer
agents.description: Early-career engineer focused on implementing well-scoped features, fixing bugs, writing tests, and learning system architecture under guidance.

agents.name: General Purpose Operator
agents.description: Versatile operator filling gaps across the engineering workflow. Handles routine maintenance, documentation updates, environment setup, and ad-hoc support.

workflows.name: Code Review Workflow
workflows.description: Standard code review process for all pull requests to maintain code quality and share knowledge.

config.description: Run CI checks including linting, unit tests, and static analysis on the feature branch
Route the PR to an appropriate reviewer based on component ownership
Reviewer examines the diff for correctness, readability, and adherence to standards
Author addresses all requested changes, updates the PR, and triggers re-review
Engineering Lead performs final approval and merges the PR to develop after all checks pass

workflows.name: Deployment Workflow
workflows.description: CI/CD-driven deployment process that automates building, testing, and deploying code to staging and production.

config.description: Build Docker image or deployment artifact from the latest commit and push to the container registry
Deploy the new artifact to the staging environment and run integration tests
Senior Engineer validates that staging changes work as expected with smoke tests
Engineering Lead approves the promotion and triggers production deployment with rolling update
Run post-deployment health checks and monitor error rates; notify the team of deployment status

workflows.name: Incident Response Workflow
workflows.description: Structured process for detecting, diagnosing, and resolving production incidents with minimal customer impact.

config.description: Automated monitoring detects the anomaly and classifies incident severity (P1/P2/P3) based on impact scope
Notify the on-call engineer via Slack and SMS; Engineering Lead assumes incident command for P1
On-call engineer investigates root cause, implements mitigation (rollback, restart, feature flag), and updates the incident channel
Automated health checks and dashboard monitoring confirm service metrics have returned to normal thresholds
Close the incident, document timeline and root cause, and create follow-up action items

workflows.name: Sprint Planning Workflow
workflows.description: Bi-weekly sprint planning process to scope, prioritize, and assign work for the upcoming iteration.

config.description: Review and refine the product backlog, remove stale items, estimate story points, ensure actionable tickets
Calculate team capacity for the sprint accounting for PTO, holidays, and a 20% unplanned buffer
Distribute backlog items across team members based on expertise, capacity, and development goals
Define 2-3 measurable sprint goals and communicate them to the full team and product stakeholders
Send sprint kickoff message with goals, task assignments, and burndown chart link to the team channel

workflows.name: Technical Debt Management Workflow
workflows.description: Systematic approach to identifying, tracking, and resolving technical debt to maintain long-term code health.

config.description: Identify technical debt items through code analysis tools, CI warnings, developer reports, and production issue patterns
Prioritize debt items by business impact, risk, and cost of delay; flag items blocking feature work
Reserve 15-20% of each sprint capacity for technical debt resolution based on the prioritized list
Engineers implement debt fixes following standard code review and deployment workflows with tests
Update tech debt dashboard with resolved items, track debt ratio trend, and report on improvement over time

semantic_memory.description: Stores structured knowledge about codebase patterns, architectural decisions, and best practices

episodic_memory.description: Records incident timelines, deployment histories, and sprint outcomes for retrospective analysis

procedural_memory.description: Caches successful command sequences, deployment scripts, and automation patterns for repeatable tasks

graph_memory.description: Not used in small team — relationships tracked via dependency graphs managed in tooling

immutable_storage.description: Git commit history and deployment audit logs serve as the immutable record of all changes

governance_rules.name: Code Review Requirement
governance_rules.description: Every pull request must have at least one approved review from a peer before merging to the develop branch. No self-merges on production-critical code.

governance_rules.name: Production Deployment Window
governance_rules.description: Production deployments are preferred during business hours (09:00-17:00 in the team timezone). Out-of-hours deployments require Engineering Lead approval.

governance_rules.name: Test Coverage Floor
governance_rules.description: All new code must maintain minimum 70% test coverage. Existing modules being modified must not decrease coverage below current baseline.

governance_rules.name: Incident Communication
governance_rules.description: All P1 and P2 incidents must be documented with a written post-incident report within 48 hours of resolution including root cause, timeline, and action items.

governance_rules.name: Secrets Management
governance_rules.description: No secrets, API keys, or credentials may be committed to version control. Use environment variables or a secrets manager. Rotate any exposed secrets within 24 hours.

kpis.name: Deployment Frequency
kpis.description: How often the team deploys to production Measured as: count per week

kpis.name: Lead Time for Changes
kpis.description: Time from code commit to production deployment Measured as: median hours

kpis.name: Change Failure Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of deployments causing a production incident Measured as: percentage

kpis.name: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
kpis.description: Average time to restore service after a production incident Measured as: minutes

kpis.name: Technical Debt Ratio
kpis.description: Estimated time to fix all known technical debt as a percentage of total development effort Measured as: percentage

kpis.name: Test Coverage
kpis.description: Percentage of codebase covered by automated tests Measured as: percentage

integrations.name: GitHub
integrations.purpose: Source code repository, pull request management, code review, and issue tracking

integrations.name: CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)
integrations.purpose: Automated build, test, and deployment pipeline triggered on PR merge and schedule

integrations.name: Monitoring (Datadog / Prometheus)
integrations.purpose: Real-time application and infrastructure monitoring with alerting on error rates, latency, and availability

integrations.name: Deployment Platform (Kubernetes / ECS)
integrations.purpose: Container orchestration platform for deploying and managing application instances

integrations.name: Slack
integrations.purpose: Team communication, incident notifications, deployment status updates, and bot interactions

operational_policies.name: On-Call Rotation
operational_policies.description: The Engineering Lead and Senior Engineer rotate weekly on-call duty. On-call engineer is responsible for initial incident response and escalation. Escalation to external support after 30 minutes for P1 incidents.

operational_policies.name: Branching Strategy
operational_policies.description: Use trunk-based development with short-lived feature branches. Main branch is always deployable. Feature flags used to protect main from incomplete features. Develop branch serves as the integration branch.

operational_policies.name: Incident Severity Definitions
operational_policies.description: P1 (Critical): Production outage affecting all users — respond within 15 minutes. P2 (High): Major feature broken for some users — respond within 30 minutes. P3 (Medium): Minor issue with workaround — respond within 4 hours.
